text:
alice.support: Hey team — ACME Prod is hitting p99 ~6s on text-generation calls from their dedicated pool eu-acme-1 since 06:10 UTC. Customer says it started after a big marketing blast.
ben.sre: thx. Any errors or 5xx?
alice.support: No 5xx, just high tail latency. We see attach/scaleup spikes in the dashboard and pool reported 100% utilization. p50 ~120ms, p95 ~1.2s, p99 ~6s.
ryan.platform: sounds like pool saturation + slow warmup. Can you paste the provisioner logs for eu-acme-1 from 06:05-06:15?
alice.support: pasted snippets below: ```
[06:07:02] pool eu-acme-1 request queued, min_pool=2, active=2, pending_attach=18
[06:07:03] provisioner: requesting new node (g4dn.xlarge) for pool eu-acme-1
[06:07:25] node bootstrapped but image pull delayed 18s
[06:07:40] runtime: model cache miss, starting quantized init (KV preload)
[06:08:30] attach complete, first token emitted 06:08:35
```
anna.runtime: that image pull + model init combo explains the extra 4-5s. Looks like many concurrent attaches caused thundering herd on cache loads.
bob?: (reaction) :face_with_thermometer:
ben.sre: Is autoscale min_pool set low? If min_pool was 2 and marketing blast sent 100 concurrent reqs, scale-up will queue and each cold attach costs ~20-30s.
alice.support: config shows min_pool=1 for that customer (they opted to save costs). They are on reserved Dedicated but kept min small.
ryan.platform: okay immediate mitigations: 1) apply temporary rate-limit (burst window) at edge for that customer to smooth spikes 2) bump min_pool to 6 for eu-acme-1 3) trigger proactive prewarm (model pre-cache) on new nodes.
maria.oncall: +1. Also recommend enabling fallback routing to hosted inference for non-sensitive paths until pool recovers. Can we safely do a partial fallback?
anna.runtime: yes, we can add a routing rule to send non-authenticated or lower-priority routes to hosted-embedding model variant. It'll reduce pressure.
alice.support: Customer approved partial fallback for analytics pipeline. I'll enable it.
ben.sre: For longer term: suggest increasing min_pool for priority customers and adding exponential backoff jitter to attach path. Also add staggered cache warmup so we don't do full KV preload for every attach concurrently.
ryan.platform: I'll open a platform ticket to add request coalescing and staggered preload in the runtime. For now I'll run a one-off script to bump min_pool and trigger prewarm: ```
# bump min pool
redwoodctl pools set eu-acme-1 --min 6 --force
# trigger prewarm on new nodes
redwoodctl pools prewarm eu-acme-1 --model acme-llama-70b-q3 --parallel 4
```
alice.support: done bumping min_pool=6 at 06:12 UTC. Customer reports p99 improving to ~1.1s at 06:25.
maria.oncall: Great. Follow-ups: - add alert for concurrent_attach > 10 and queue_length > 20 - document playbook for marketing-driven bursts - billing note: consumer opted to keep min low to save costs; need to flag tradeoffs in support playbook.
ben.sre: I'll file PR for attach jitter and doc the fallbacks. Also recommend a 24h retention check on node image registry to reduce image-pull delays.
alice.support: marking customer incident resolved (they're still monitoring). Thanks all.
provisioner-bot: [06:30] Auto-scaling event: pool eu-acme-1 scaled to 8 nodes.
ryan.platform: Filing follow-up ticket: PLT-7521 "prewarm + throttle playbook for priority dedicated pools" and assigning to eng-runtime.
anna.runtime: I'll take PLT-7521. Plan: incremental prewarm, async KV load, and add a mode to prefetch model shards before productive attach.
alice.support: Closing thread. Will reopen if customer sees new regressions. :thumbsup:
